races.name: Kettle Produce Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Pergamon
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins at 2m on Good make this an on-paper fit, and Jennie Candlish's yard is firing at 2/23 in the 14-day window; held up in a prominent role naturally but the STYLE_FIT tag signals it operates best further forward than pure lead — here the lead comes to it naturally, which is the key angle, though watch the TP headgear for clues on freshness after 53 days off.

runners_data.name: Pure Gold
runners_data.note: Lisa Harrison's yard has had just one runner in the past fortnight, keeping profile modest, but Pure Gold's win on Good ground at 16f is directly relevant; a natural prominent racer whose best form at this trip and going reads well, though the fall in recent form (1F75-4) and soft-ground preference shown in the sim-going record (2W6P from 15 runs on similar conditions) introduces doubt.

runners_data.name: Ravenscraig Castle
runners_data.note: Iain Jardine's string is active (4/26 in 14 days) and Danny McMenamin is a sharp jockey for this track, but this horse's natural racing style is prominent — it is mapped to midfield here only because Pergamon and Pure Gold compress that space, so it may race closer than the map shows if gaps appear early; the hood and a recent 25-day turnaround suggest fitness is not a concern, though soft-ground form dominates its history.

runners_data.name: Just Dottie
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up performer whose Good-ground record at 2m is consistent (5/16f/GOO, 4/12f/GOO, 6/16f/GOO), and William Maggs's 3lb claim brings the weight to a manageable level; needs the pace to be quick enough to reel in the front rank at Perth, which is unlikely given Pergamon's control, making this a ground-neutral but pace-dependent profile that the current shape may not serve.

runners_data.name: Tigress Lilly
runners_data.note: A winless record across five starts on Good or Soft at 2m tells its own story (form: 5700-6), and the tongue-tie entry has not unlocked improvement yet; Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore's dual-trainer operation is capable, and the 25-day gap is not concerning, but this horse looks outpaced in the handicap and needs a complete collapse in the front rank to feature.

runners_data.name: Interchangeable
runners_data.note: John Dixon trains and rides this horse through his amateur jockey (Mr John Dixon, 7lb claim), a family operation with no recent runners to gauge stable form; a true hold-up horse whose recent 6th at 2m on Good mirrors this exact race condition, and while a 3rd at 2m2f on Good (sim-going) shows it can stay and jump, it is mapped forward of its natural position and will need a seismic shift in race dynamics to reach the principals from the rear.

races.paceDynamic: Pergamon is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only Pure Gold as a genuine prominent threat to press early, is likely to bowl along at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over this sharp 2m Perth circuit without being seriously harassed. Pure Gold will attempt to track closely, but the pace is unlikely to be frantic — Pergamon's rider William Shanahan can dictate terms and control the tempo from the front. This shape creates a race that strongly favours horses racing prominently or at worst in mid-division, as the even gallop over a flat, right-handed track will not produce enough late acceleration for genuine hold-up horses to close from off the pace. This field holds more prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Ravenscraig Castle is a genuine prominent racer who must compete for limited early real estate, while Interchangeable is a true hold-up horse shuffled forward on the map and unlikely to be closer to the pace than its natural style suggests.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Pergamon Controls Cleanly
scenarios.trigger: If Pergamon bowls along uncontested and Pure Gold tracks without applying real pressure, the race is run at a steady-to-honest tempo that suits the race leader.
scenarios.body: If Pergamon bowls along uncontested and Pure Gold tracks without applying real pressure, the race is run at a steady-to-honest tempo that suits the race leader.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Sneak Into Contention
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace compresses the field and a prominent-to-mid tracker makes steady headway from three out without needing a sprint finish.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace compresses the field and a prominent-to-mid tracker makes steady headway from three out without needing a sprint finish.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pure Gold Challenges Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pure Gold travels strongly throughout and mounts a sustained challenge from the second-last, turning a tactical race into a two-horse duel.
scenarios.body: If Pure Gold travels strongly throughout and mounts a sustained challenge from the second-last, turning a tactical race into a two-horse duel.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos at Steady Pace
scenarios.trigger: If multiple runners interfere at a hurdle or Pergamon makes a critical jumping error, scrambling the expected order.
scenarios.body: If multiple runners interfere at a hurdle or Pergamon makes a critical jumping error, scrambling the expected order.

watchPoints.text: Ravenscraig Castle may push forward from its mapped midfield position early — if it does, watch for a three-way scrap for prominent berths with Pergamon and Pure Gold that inflates the pace and fundamentally changes the race shape.
Pergamon carries 168lbs after 53 days off — any sign of jumping fatigue or a hesitant jump at the cross-fence hurdle could bring Pure Gold and the tracking pair into immediate contention.

Pure Gold's recent form string (1F75-4) includes a fall and three poor efforts; if it races prominently but comes under pressure before the home turn, it could interfere with Pergamon's rhythm rather than track it cleanly.

Just Dottie and Interchangeable are both genuine hold-up horses that need the front end to tire — on Good ground at a flat circuit like Perth, the pace is unlikely to be brutal enough to create that scenario, so both require an added luck element to win.

William Maggs (3lb claim, Just Dottie) and Mr John Dixon (7lb claim, Interchangeable) are inexperienced riders in a race where positional discipline early will matter — watch both for whether they settle their mounts or use up energy fighting for position the horses would not naturally seek.

races.name: Secure Air Parks Edinburgh Airport Parking Handicap Chase (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Wasdell Dundalk
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer for Lisa Harrison with sound Good-ground form (won at 24f on Good), McMenamin up and 25 days fresh — watch him from mid-division in a compressed finish, though the moderate pace may bring him into play sooner than his trainer intends.

runners_data.name: Gunnery Sergeant
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner, Bowen takes the mount for Gordon Elliott whose stable is firing (7/53 in 14 days); his sim-going record on Good is modest (0W) but uncontested control at Perth over 2m4f on this surface hands him a major positional gift that statistics alone understate.

runners_data.name: Moodofthemoment
runners_data.note: Won on Good ground at 20f and placed at 22f, returning quickly (11 days) in first-time hood for David Thompson — Quinlan can park him off the leader's quarters and his recent winning run (1st last time) makes him the most dangerous challenger to the favourite from a tracking position.

runners_data.name: Garde Des Champs
runners_data.note: Russell & Scudamore runner with solid course-form (13 runs on Good, 1W7P) and Alan Doyle claiming 3lbs, but at age 10 and a true hold-up type who has been pushed into midfield by the congested rear, his chance is structurally squeezed in what looks a falsely-run contest.

runners_data.name: Kinbara Firstdraft
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 7-year-old for Leonard Kerr with Conor Rabbitt also claiming 3lbs; a natural closer who sits in midfield by necessity rather than design, and with a poor recent record (no win in last five, modest sim-going figures), the style displacement genuinely undermines his prospects here.

runners_data.name: Button Rock
runners_data.note: Elliott's second string, a natural hold-up horse who has not won in five attempts on Good or Heavy ground; 51 days off and a worrying 14-runner finish last time out — his redistribution to midfield adds to an already difficult profile on a going and trip that has not brought out the best in him.

runners_data.name: Jiair Madrik
runners_data.note: Listed as NON-RUNNER — if declared and taking its place, a horse with back-to-back wins on Good (1/20f, 1/21f) and a genuine hold-up pedigree (hg:ht) who performs best when able to sweep late; in this compressed single-pace shape, however, getting a true hold-up run would be structurally difficult.

races.paceDynamic: Gunnery Sergeant is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner field and, with no genuine rival to press him early, Sean Bowen can dictate a controlled, economical gallop from the outset over 2m4f on Good ground at Perth. That lone-leader scenario creates a slowly-run or evenly-run race in which the prominent position is virtually gift-wrapped, and horses who can travel smoothly just off the pace will be best placed to exploit a sustainable tempo. The field nominally contains a cluster of hold-up types — Garde Des Champs, Kinbara Firstdraft, Button Rock and Jiair Madrik are all true closers but are mapped to midfield because there are more hold-up horses than the shape has room for at the rear, meaning at least some of them will be forced to race closer than ideal. This race shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently or pick up from mid-division in a run-to-post contest, with genuine deep closers at a structural disadvantage given the single-pace setter and the likelihood of a muddling, compressed finish.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Gunnery Sergeant Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Gunnery Sergeant bowls along uncontested and Bowen dictates a comfortable gallop, allowing him to quicken off his own pace in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Gunnery Sergeant bowls along uncontested and Bowen dictates a comfortable gallop, allowing him to quicken off his own pace in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Types Storm Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses or Gunnery Sergeant weakens dramatically after the last, opening a gap for closers who have tracked efficiently.
scenarios.body: If the pace collapses or Gunnery Sergeant weakens dramatically after the last, opening a gap for closers who have tracked efficiently.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse travelling just behind Gunnery Sergeant attacks two out and the leader cannot repel a sustained challenge.
scenarios.body: If a horse travelling just behind Gunnery Sergeant attacks two out and the leader cannot repel a sustained challenge.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Order
scenarios.trigger: If early jumping errors or a fall shuffle the race dramatically and a genuine hold-up horse finds a clean run from the rear.
scenarios.body: If early jumping errors or a fall shuffle the race dramatically and a genuine hold-up horse finds a clean run from the rear.

watchPoints.text: Gunnery Sergeant has zero wins or places in seven sim-going runs on Good, so watch whether Bowen elects to increase the gallop mid-race rather than crawl — a change of tactics could compress the field earlier than expected.

Moodofthemoment returned just 11 days ago and carries a hood; watch his jumping under Quinlan, as any early blunder from close to the leader would immediately compromise the main anti-favourite scenario.

With four hold-up horses all forced forward against their natural style, watch the early-race jostling between Garde Des Champs, Kinbara Firstdraft, Button Rock and the field for position — any crowding at the first few fences could cause a significant incident.

Jiair Madrik is listed as a non-runner — confirm at the final declarations stage, as its removal reduces the hold-up cluster and marginally improves the run of race for the remaining mid-division types.

Good ground throughout the card at Perth is confirmed consistent — no bias concern, but watch how quickly the pace develops after the first fence; if Gunnery Sergeant is given a completely unchallenged lead by fence two, the race shape is effectively locked in for Scenario A.

races.name: PWA Architecture Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Sonyourastar
runners_data.note: A hold-up horse for Olly Murphy whose recent form (8-8 in two Good-ground runs) is worrying, and the finishing-fade flag compounds the concern; 41 days off, 168lbs, and a record of 0W0P on similar going makes this a hard horse to trust.|

runners_data.name: Fourofakind
runners_data.note: 102 days off the track is a significant absence flag for Lizzie Quinlan's seven-year-old; his best form sits at 20f on Soft and he has placed twice from 15 similar-going runs, but this trip on Good ground and the long break make him speculative at best.|

runners_data.name: Bayonetta
runners_data.note: A genuine prominent racer with an outstanding record of 11 runs in similar going conditions and six places to show for it; Benjamin Macey (5lb claim) rides and the eight-year-old has placed at 22f and 24f on Good, suggesting the 2m4f trip is well within range.|

runners_data.name: Betteryouthanme
runners_data.note: Ran just 11 days ago and showed a win at 16f on Good ground in recent form, stepping up to 2m4f here for R Mike Smith; the prominent style keeps him in the front group and the trainer has two runners placed in 23-day window, suggesting horses are fit.|

runners_data.name: Top Flight Century
runners_data.note: A five-year-old prominent type who won at 20f on Good and has placed four times in 15 similar-going runs; the 5lb claimer Joshua Thompson is a notable booking and the 11-day turnaround mirrors stablemate Betteryouthanme, suggesting the yard is in a productive spell.|

runners_data.name: Lenko
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's four-year-old is lightly raced and flagged as a hold-up horse who fades in the finish — a concerning combination; 48 days off, 0W0P in three Good-ground runs and a form line of 6-0-0 makes him one to watch from a market perspective rather than a selection angle.|

runners_data.name: Fairly Fulling
runners_data.note: Susan Corbett's eight-year-old ran 23 days ago and has placed four times at this trip on Soft; the tp headgear is worn again and the Good ground is a potential step up in underfoot conditions that could stretch her stamina, but her prominent style keeps her in the race shape.|

runners_data.name: King Kodiak
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse for the Bewley yard whose natural race position is at the rear; placed here in the midfield only because the field is overloaded with closers, and with a STYLE_FIT of 0.91 he is structurally disadvantaged in a slowly-run race — his one place in 12 similar-going runs reflects this.|

runners_data.name: Malangen
runners_data.note: The lone confirmed front-runner whose recent form of five places from 15 Good-ground runs and a win at this trip show genuine suitability; Peter Kavanagh can dictate unchallenged, and at 11 years old his ability to sustain a rhythm is proven even if a winning finish has become harder to manufacture.|

runners_data.name: Breaking Ground
runners_data.note: A five-year-old true hold-up horse pushed into the midfield map position due to field congestion at the rear; the finishing-fade flag and a form line of P-5-0-0-8 with 0W0P across seven similar-going attempts makes him deeply unfancied regardless of scenario — STYLE_FIT of 0.90 is appropriate.|

runners_data.name: Dreamings Free
runners_data.note: 192 days off the track is a very long absence for Maurice Barnes' six-year-old, who is a genuine hold-up type now shown in midfield for structural reasons rather than racing preference; has placed twice at 24f on Good and Soft, so the trip is not the issue, but the near-seven-month break is.|

races.paceDynamic: Malangen is the sole confirmed front-runner and will lead from the off at a sustainable gallop on Good ground over 2m4f at Perth, a track that rewards front-rank position but does not inherently punish a controlled tempo. With no dedicated rival to press him, Peter Kavanagh can dictate terms at a pace that suits, meaning the race is unlikely to develop into a true stamina test — the emphasis falls on those close to the pace rather than those coming from deep. Prominent racers Bayonetta, Betteryouthanme, Top Flight Century and Fairly Fulling are all genuine pace-forwardly types who will sit within striking range without having to burn fuel chasing a runaway leader. This race shape strongly favours the prominent, close-tracking profile: runners who can settle just off Malangen's shoulder and pounce in the straight without having to produce a sustained finish from off the pace. The field carries more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate naturally — King Kodiak, Breaking Ground and Dreamings Free are genuine rear-of-field types redistributed to midfield, meaning they are unlikely to secure their preferred position and must be discounted in shapes that demand a late, wide-open gallop.

watchPoints.text: Bayonetta's record of 11 runs in similar going conditions and six places makes her the key prominent tracker to watch — if she settles smoothly just off Malangen, she is the most likely beneficiary of Scenario A.|

Malangen's uncontested lead must be monitored closely from the first hurdle — if no rival challenges him through the early stages, Peter Kavanagh can build a rhythm that makes him very difficult to pass and Scenario B becomes live.|

King Kodiak, Breaking Ground and Dreamings Free are all genuine rear-of-field types who cannot get their natural position in this race shape; if the pace suddenly lifts and they find cover unexpectedly, Scenario C becomes more dangerous than its 14% probability suggests.|

Betteryouthanme ran only 11 days ago and Top Flight Century also returns on the same tight turnaround — watch the market move on both R Mike Smith runners as a guide to which is the yard's primary hope in this race.|

Lenko's Gordon Elliott booking via Danny McMenamin and the yard's T14 strike rate of 9/65 is worth noting — Elliott sends horses north sparingly and this four-year-old may be better than his bare form figures suggest, even if the hold-up style with a fade flag is structurally awkward.|

races.name: Horizon Parking UK's Leading Parking Company Handicap Chase

runners_data.name: The Flying Poet
runners_data.note: Top-rated runner at OR 105 with strong Good-ground form (sim-going 9/10) and a recent winning profile; genuinely prominent by style but leads here by default given the field — Sean Bowen's positive riding style suits dictating, though the 3m trip is a step up from his recent 2m3-4f efforts.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Blizzard
runners_data.note: A genuine hold-up horse whose recent form figures (2PP-57) suggest patchy reliability; Derek Fox rides for Russell/Scudamore who have only one runner in a 14-day window, and the Good ground suits — needs the pace to develop to get a strong-enough gallop to close into.

runners_data.name: Get A Superstar
runners_data.note: Two recent wins at Goodwood on Good give him strong credentials on today's surface; a natural prominent type with Charlie Hammond up for a yard without a recent winner strike, and he steps up in trip from 22f to 24f but his form at this sort of distance is solid.

runners_data.name: Thehairyfella
runners_data.note: An 11-year-old hold-up horse for Gordon Elliott, whose strong trainer strike rate (11/49 in 14 days) is a notable positive; has course-distance experience and his sim-going record (13/15) is excellent, but he will need the pace to be genuine to deliver his finish and needs to be taken on trust at his age.

runners_data.name: Burgundy Man
runners_data.note: A natural prominent racer with tack headgear (tp) who has shown enough in Good-ground races to be competitive; Nathan Moscrop is a 7lb claimer for a trainer without recent form, and his most recent runs show he stays without always finding a turn of foot at the finish.

runners_data.name: Defying Gravity
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type mapped to midfield for display purposes given the field shape — his genuine style means he will sit last or near-last and needs a strong gallop he is unlikely to get; the fade-in-finish flag is a concern, and Conor Rabbitt's 3lb claim does little to offset the structural disadvantage.

runners_data.name: Twp Stori
runners_data.note: Naturally prominent by style but this field's numbers push him out of that position; Benjamin Macey's 5lb claim helps on weight, but his sim-going record is weak (2/15) and back-to-back thirds at this level suggest he finds winning hard — racing out of his preferred slot makes this harder still.

races.paceDynamic: The Flying Poet is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pressure expected to emerge from the seven-runner field, is likely to dictate at a comfortable, controlled gallop over this 3m trip on Good ground at Perth. Get A Superstar and Burgundy Man are genuine prominent types who will push forward to track the leader, creating a small, organised lead group rather than a contested head-to-head for the front. The field holds more prominent runners than can all secure their natural position — Twp Stori is a natural prominent racer who will likely find himself shuffled back behind the front two or three, while Defying Gravity, a genuine hold-up type, is mapped to midfield for display purposes only. With a sustainable, uncontested pace set by The Flying Poet, this race shape strongly favours horses that can travel prominently and produce a resolute jump-by-jump challenge in the home straight, rather than late closers who need a truly strong gallop to get into the race.

scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If The Flying Poet dictates an uncontested tempo and the prominent trackers travel smoothly in behind.
scenarios.body: If The Flying Poet dictates an uncontested tempo and the prominent trackers travel smoothly in behind.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Leader Outstayed Late
scenarios.trigger: If The Flying Poet's lead is too exposed and a hold-up runner picks up the pieces close home.
scenarios.body: If The Flying Poet's lead is too exposed and a hold-up runner picks up the pieces close home.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Heats Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If Burgundy Man or Twp Stori press The Flying Poet more than expected through the middle stages.
scenarios.body: If Burgundy Man or Twp Stori press The Flying Poet more than expected through the middle stages.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Incident Shapes Race
scenarios.trigger: If a faller, unseated, or significant jumping error disrupts the lead group and reshuffles the pack.

watchPoints.text: The Flying Poet shapes as the controlling influence — if he gets to the third-last with a clear lead and jumping fluently, the race is likely already decided; watch for any jockey challenge from Get A Superstar from the home turn as the most likely threat.

Twp Stori's natural desire to race prominently may cause him to push forward regardless of instructions and briefly contest the lead with The Flying Poet, which could inject an unplanned mid-race surge that tests all runners' stamina.

Defying Gravity is flagged for fading in the finish — if the race is run at the predicted controlled tempo, there is a real risk he has nothing left to give when the pressure comes in the straight, despite any good early position.

Thehairyfella carries the most experience at 11 years old and has a strong sim-going profile — watch whether Danny McMenamin positions him closer than his hold-up tag suggests in the early stages, which would be the signal he is travelling well enough to mount a genuine challenge.

The trainer angle on Gordon Elliott (11 winners from 49 runners in 14 days) for Thehairyfella is worth noting as a cold form pointer — Elliott runners arriving in form often outrun market expectations in northern summer handicaps.

races.name: AEJ Facilities Management Handicap Hurdle

runners_data.name: Maggies Boy
runners_data.note: Won over 21f on Good last time, handles this ground well (11/15 similar-going record), and from a hold-up base could creep into the race if Creadan Grace sets the pace strongly enough to create a target; Sean Quinlan is a savvy judge of pace.

runners_data.name: Les's Legacy
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old whose form figures on Good are respectable but whose soft-ground record is markedly worse; Nathan Moscrop takes the ride for a trainer whose 14-day strike rate is modest, and the step up to 3m from recent 2m starts is untested in current form.

runners_data.name: Creadan Grace
runners_data.note: Gordon Elliott's six-year-old has a strong Good-ground profile (9/11) and won over 24f in that context; Robert Dunne partners a horse whose prominent style is perfectly suited to slotting in behind The Best Way and pouncing from the last, making this the most naturally positioned challenger.

runners_data.name: The Best Way
runners_data.note: Lone front-runner who will control the tempo entirely unopposed; won last time out over a shorter trip on Soft and now faces a 3m test on Good, which is a slight unknown, but the licence to bowl along at his own pace is a significant tactical advantage.

runners_data.name: Dalileo
runners_data.note: Eleven-year-old with a decent Good-ground record (11/15) and course-relevant staying form, though he tends to race in hold-up or midfield slots; Peter Kavanagh will need him to travel efficiently as the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to bring him into it from far back.

runners_data.name: Loro White
runners_data.note: Olly Murphy's five-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse by nature — won on Soft over 20f and has ability — but is mapped into midfield here because the rear of the field is overcrowded; Sean Bowen is a high-class ally, though racing outside his comfort zone tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: C'Mon So
runners_data.note: Five-year-old for Lucinda Russell and Michael Scudamore with a consistent hold-up profile and a form string showing repeated mid-pack finishes on Good; bumped into midfield by the field's composition rather than by choice, which means Derek Fox will need an atypically forward ride to make an impact.

runners_data.name: Prince Nino
runners_data.note: Won over 20f on Soft last time, but his Good-ground record reads 7/15 and his natural rear-of-field style is squeezed out by the volume of similar horses in this field; Alan Doyle's 3lb claim helps on weight, but 50 days off and a style-fit discount combine to make this a big ask.

runners_data.name: Myfavouritesister
runners_data.note: Brian Hughes partners a seven-year-old who has raced prominently in headgear before but whose recent form (P, 7, 5) is uninspiring; placed into midfield against her natural inclination, and 11 days since her last run is a short turnaround with little to suggest she can reverse that trend here.

runners_data.name: King Gold Boy
runners_data.note: Five-year-old returning after 206 days off for a trainer with a 0/0 14-day record; two career P finishes in the form string and a natural hold-up style displaced into midfield are compounding negatives, and the lengthy absence makes it very hard to assess current fitness.

races.paceDynamic: The Best Way is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to pressure them, Danny McMenamin can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front over this 3m trip on Good ground at Perth. The field is deceptively packed with hold-up types — Loro White, C'Mon So, Prince Nino, Myfavouritesister and King Gold Boy are all natural rearward racers — meaning the prominent slots behind The Best Way are likely to be filled by Creadan Grace and possibly Maggies Boy or Dalileo pushing forward from their usual positions. Because so many genuine hold-up horses cannot all secure their preferred berth, the race is unlikely to truly collapse into a strong-pace scenario where closers are automatically served; instead, the likely steady-to-fair gallop set by The Best Way will suit horses who can travel prominently and quicken at the business end. This shape strongly favours prominent racers and those closest to the pace who can strike from two out, rather than the deep hold-up brigade who will need a lot to go right to get competitive.

scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prompt Strike
scenarios.trigger: If The Best Way sets a fair but unchallenged gallop and the race is decided by those racing in the first three or four positions from the home turn.
scenarios.body: If The Best Way sets a fair but unchallenged gallop and the race is decided by those racing in the first three or four positions from the home turn.

scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and a hold-up-turned-midfield horse delivers a sustained run from the back of the front group.
scenarios.body: If the pace is slightly stronger than expected and a hold-up-turned-midfield horse delivers a sustained run from the back of the front group.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Outstays All
scenarios.trigger: If The Best Way jumps fluently throughout and the pace is so steady that no rival can close the gap from three out.
scenarios.body: If The Best Way jumps fluently throughout and the pace is so steady that no rival can close the gap from three out.

scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops at a truly searching gallop that strings the field out and the deepest hold-up runners find sufficient daylight to deliver a run.

watchPoints.text: Creadan Grace's jumping is worth monitoring closely — Gordon Elliott's prominent racer is the horse best placed to attack The Best Way from three out, and any jumping error in the home straight would dramatically shift the finish.
